rationale: Round 3 plan (replaces round 2's 6 copies per plate). Stock 0.20mm QUALITY @MK3 + Prusament PETG (filament_type PETG = print_requirements; 250 °C, first layer 240, bed 90/85, fan 30-50 %: inside 230-250 / 80-90 and the skill's PETG range, so not overridden). Overrides meet print_requirements.json exactly as strength modelled the tibia: 4 perimeters (1.67 mm), 5 top / 5 bottom layers (1.0 mm skins), 50 % gyroid, 0.2 mm layers. Elephant-foot 0.2 pairs with the 0.4 mm bed chamfer and keeps the bed face flat: it is the back face that runs 3.1 mm off the femur (spec §2: nothing may stand proud of it), and it carries the horn pocket. Copies 3, the same file printed on 2 plates = spec §7 (6 tibias, 3 h per batch; sliced 1.93 h): round 2's 6 per plate took 3.86 h, over the limit. The brief's 4 + 2 would need two different G-code files, and a job holds one part.gcode, so 3 + 3 prints the same approved file twice. Orientation is in the STL (brief): flat, horn pocket on the bed. No library rows (materials.csv and lessons.md are empty), so no flow, temperature or xy compensation overrides. Seam: aligned (stated explicitly), so it stays in one vertical line instead of scattering round the foot tip and the horn pocket. Checked in the G-code: the outline's seam is on the Ø18 hub's -y edge at x 1, the others at the horn pocket's arm tip and in the clamp hole. None is on the back face or at the governing section (x 13, loaded out of plane, so its stress is in the top and bottom skins). Brim: none (brim_width 0): PETG barely warps on a 7 mm flat plate, and a brim would leave a lip on the back face.
